text: I am Dr. Agent. You have reported progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed any specific triggers for the pain, such as injury, repetitive use, or exposure to cold? Additionally, can you describe the exact location of the tenderness and whether there is any visible redness or warmth in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Gamekeeper's thumb injury (Ulnar Collateral Ligament tear) of the right ring finger.

Please note: While your description mentions the "ring finger," the mechanism of injury (forceful pull on a finger while playing football) is classic for a Ulnar Collateral Ligament (UCL) tear, which most commonly affects the *thumb* (Gamekeeper's thumb). If the injury is truly to the ring finger, this could be a similar collateral ligament injury or a fracture. I will proceed with the diagnosis based on the mechanism provided, but please confirm if you meant your thumb was injured rather than your ring finger.

REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray of the right hand (AP and Lateral views) to rule out fracture or dislocation.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
